notes:
## 1.0.7 — 2026-08-02

### The Archive becomes a visual library
- **Browse, don't just index.** The Archive tool is now a full browser:
  best-moment preview grids for every clip, hover-scrub, Apple-Photos-style
  zoom from years down to single clips, moments as tiles, and a constellation
  map. Bulk-edit shoot dates and tags across a selection.
- **Analysis lives on the drive.** Every stage an archive (or project) clip
  completes is written to a catalog beside the footage and merges back into
  the library — a synced-database mishap can no longer cost analysis.
- **Weekend runs.** `python -m dvea.archive_run "<root>"` analyzes a whole
  drive with Cut Valet closed; the next launch offers a one-click import.
- **Watch it work.** Per-stage progress bars (purple → blue → green) in the
  index dialog and on the browser's right rail. Start an index, close the
  window — it keeps running. Close the main Cut Valet window too and watch
  from the archive window; "Open Cut Valet" brings the app back.
- **The AI editor can reach it.** Search everything ever indexed (opt-in
  library scope), and archive roots are one checkbox in the plan window's
  footage menu.

### Ingest: eyes before brains
- A new preview stage builds 25-frame contact sheets and SigLIP best-moment
  posters minutes after copy (toggle in Settings → processing); the Clip
  Inspector hover-scrubs from them with no extra setup.
- A Metadata row in the queue panel shows the exif/sidecar work between
  "copy done" and analysis — the stretch that used to look idle.

### AI editing
- Content-aware cut points from dense timeline events; "/" command menu in
  the chat; b-roll picks the best-looking window inside a match and lands
  overlays on their words; a VLM vote chooses among candidate windows; the
  planner can pick or generate graphics; text recall widens b-roll
  candidates; cover scopes to the current project ("from the library"
  widens deliberately).
- GPT-5.x and Gemini tool loops fixed (Responses API); reasoning stays on.

### Fixes & polish
- Find-a-song no longer blocks the app; stem separation; remembered drop
  folders; the local AI engine stops with the app and sizes itself from
  model metadata; analysis no longer parks on the GPU; missing assets are
  caught before a render; plus a full post-ship stability audit (six abort
  paths fixed) and safer database plumbing throughout.
